title: Open-source AI coding tools to evaluate
summary: A conditional shortlist based on project license evidence, model boundaries and current maintenance signals.

facts.value: The public repository identifies an Apache-2.0 license.

facts.value: The public repository identifies an Apache-2.0 license.

facts.value: The repository identifies Apache 2.0 but also states that the upstream repository is read-only and no longer actively maintained.

sections.heading: Treat the shortlist as due diligence
paragraphs: Aider's repository documents terminal pair programming and Git integration. Cline's repository describes an SDK, IDE extension and CLI. These are workflow candidates, not benchmark winners; test the same small repository task and review the resulting changes.

sections.heading: Separate code license from the model stack
paragraphs: A project license does not license a model's weights, a hosted provider, an extension marketplace or the code and prompts sent to those services. Check every layer against the intended commercial and privacy requirements.

sections.heading: Handle Continue as a lifecycle exception
paragraphs: Continue's upstream README retains an Apache-2.0 license statement but says that the repository is read-only and no longer actively maintained. Do not include it in a production recommendation until the exact installed package, publisher, updates and security response are confirmed.

sections.heading: Run a reversible trial
paragraphs: Use a branch, synthetic data and a real acceptance test. Compare review effort, model/provider cost, update cadence and recovery steps. Keep a fallback until the tool and its external model path satisfy the team's requirements.

verdict: Aider and Cline are conditional candidates for evaluation based on the linked repository evidence. Continue remains a maintenance-risk exception; no comparative performance result has been measured.
bestFor: Developers who want to inspect source and license terms while evaluating AI coding workflows
notFor: Teams treating an open-source client license as proof that every model, service or data path is open or offline
migration: Pin the client version and model endpoint, preserve a human-reviewed fallback, and recheck license and maintenance evidence before upgrading.
gaps: Confirm the license of the exact installed package and any model or hosted service; repository license evidence alone is insufficient.
Continue's distribution, current maintenance, publisher and security response need confirmation before any production recommendation.
No hands-on comparison or model performance test has been performed.
